references.text: Isaiah warns against those who stagger from wine and strong drink, so that priests and prophets stumble. A parallel to Jesus' warning about the heart being weighed down by intoxication and drunkenness ([ref:Jes 28:7|Isaiah 28:7]).

Proverbs warns against being among drunkards and gluttons, which reflects Jesus' exhortation not to let the heart be weighed down by drunkenness and debauchery ([ref:Ordsp 23:20-21|Proverbs 23:20-21]).
Paul exhorts believers to walk properly, not in revelry and drunkenness, which directly mirrors Jesus' warning against intoxication and drunkenness ([ref:Rom 13:13|Romans 13:13]).

Paul describes the day of the Lord as coming like a thief in the night, suddenly overtaking people, paralleling Jesus' warning that "that day" will come unexpectedly ([ref:1 Tess 5:2-3|1 Thessalonians 5:2-3]).

Paul exhorts believers to stay awake and be sober, not sleeping like others, in agreement with Jesus' warning about vigilance and not letting the heart be weighed down ([ref:1 Tess 5:6-7|1 Thessalonians 5:6-7]).

Jesus describes the wicked servant who begins to eat and drink with drunkards, and whose master comes on a day he does not expect – paralleling the warning in Luke 21:34 that the day will not come unexpectedly ([ref:Matt 24:48-50|Matthew 24:48-50]).

Jesus' parable of the servant who begins to eat, drink, and get drunk, while the master comes unexpectedly – a close parallel to the warning against drunkenness and the unexpected day ([ref:Luk 12:45-46|Luke 12:45-46]).

Peter exhorts believers to be sober-minded and self-controlled for prayer, which corresponds to Jesus' warning not to let the heart be weighed down by worldly cares and drunkenness ([ref:1 Pet 4:7|1 Peter 4:7]).

In the parable of the sower, Jesus describes those who are choked by life's worries, riches, and pleasures – paralleling the warning against "life's worries" (μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς) in Luke 21:34 ([ref:Luk 8:14|Luke 8:14]).
Mark's version of the parable of the sower mentions that "the cares of this world" choke the word, paralleling the warning against life's worries ([ref:Mark 4:19|Mark 4:19]).
Jesus exhorts his disciples to be on guard, stay awake, and pray, for they do not know when the time will come – a close parallel to the exhortation in Luke 21:34 ([ref:Mark 13:33|Mark 13:33]).

Isaiah speaks of people who are drunk without wine, staggered without strong drink, because the Lord has poured out upon them a spirit of deep sleep. A spiritual dullness that mirrors the warning about the heart being weighed down ([ref:Jes 29:9-10|Isaiah 29:9-10]).
